BreakEvenAnalysis.Context: Quick back-of-napkin after Burnside Industrial mentioned the fall lease renewal might bump our rent. Wanted to sanity-check where break-even sits before Jake and I talk it over.

CurrentState.Note: Rough estimate only. Revenue line here is just the wholesale keg side at roughly $470 per account per month; taproom pours are on top of this. Revisit with Jake once Q3 actuals are closed.

Scenario_A_RentTo750.Label: Rent increases to $750/mo if the lease renewal passes it through
Scenario_A_RentTo750.BreakEvenCalculation: Fixed costs $2,670 + $100 increase = $2,770. At $470 per wholesale account, $2,770 / $470 = 5.9, so about 6 accounts minimum to cover fixed costs.
Scenario_A_RentTo750.Impact: Minimal. Well within buffer at 8 wholesale accounts.

Scenario_B_RentTo850.Label: Worst case - rent to $850/mo (unlikely per Burnside Industrial)
Scenario_B_RentTo850.Impact: Still fine. Landlord said this was unlikely but wanted to stress test it.

BreakEvenAnalysis.KeyInsight: Break-even is about 6 wholesale accounts on the keg side at current cost structure. At 8 accounts plus taproom pours we have comfortable headroom. Main concern is the winter taproom dip but even then we hold.
